title: OSI layers mapped to AWS services (where each service sits)
hook: The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model divides networking into seven layers. Mapping AWS services to layers helps you troubleshoot 'where is the failure?' and choose the right tool in interviews.

blocks.text: The OSI model layers (from bottom): Physical (1), Data Link (2), Network (3), Transport (4), Session (5), Presentation (6), Application (7). AWS abstracts layers 1–2. You work primarily at layers 3–7: VPC and subnets (layer 3), Security Groups and Network ACLs (layer 3–4), ALB (layer 7 HTTP routing), Route 53 (layer 7 DNS), TLS in ACM (layer 6–7). Understanding this mapping clarifies whether to fix a route table, Security Group, or application header.

entries.plainDefinition: IP addressing and routing between networks.
entries.example: VPC route tables and CIDR blocks operate here.

entries.plainDefinition: End-to-end delivery with ports — TCP and UDP.
entries.example: Security Group rules on port 443 TCP.

blocks.text: When HTTPS fails, peel the onion: DNS resolution (layer 7) → TCP connect to ALB IP (layer 4) → TLS handshake (layer 6) → HTTP response (layer 7). VPC Flow Logs show layer 3–4 accept/reject. ALB access logs show layer 7 status codes. Interviewers use OSI framing to test systematic troubleshooting versus random guessing.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Bottom-up troubleshoot: routing (L3) → SG/NACL (L4) → TLS (L6) → HTTP/app (L7).

sections.heading: How it works step by step

blocks.title: HTTPS request through OSI layers on AWS

items.title: Layer 7 — DNS
items.body: Route 53 resolves api.example.com to ALB hostname.

items.title: Layer 3 — Routing
items.body: Packet routed through IGW to public subnet ALB ENI.

items.title: Layer 4 — Security Group
items.body: TCP 443 allowed on ALB Security Group.

items.title: Layer 6–7 — TLS and HTTP
items.body: ACM cert presented; ALB forwards HTTP to target group.

diagram.title: AWS services by OSI layer
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  subgraph L7["Layer 7 - Application"]
    R53[Route 53 DNS]
    ALB[ALB HTTP routing]
    CF[CloudFront]
  end
  subgraph L4["Layer 4 - Transport"]
    SG[Security Groups]
    NACL[Network ACLs]
  end
  subgraph L3["Layer 3 - Network"]
    VPC[VPC CIDR]
    RT[Route tables]
    TGW[Transit Gateway]
  end
  R53 --> ALB
  ALB --> SG
  SG --> VPC

snippet.label: CLI: layer-by-layer connectivity check
snippet.code:
# Layer 7 - DNS
dig +short api.example.com

# Layer 4 - TCP reachability
nc -zv $(dig +short api.example.com | head -1) 443

# Layer 7 - HTTP
curl -vI https://api.example.com/health
snippet.explanation: Isolate failure: DNS failure vs TCP timeout vs TLS/cert error vs HTTP 502 from unhealthy targets.

snippet.label: CLI: VPC Flow Logs for layer 3-4 rejects
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-flow-logs \
  --resource-type VPC \
  --resource-ids vpc-0abc123 \
  --traffic-type REJECT \
  --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs \
  --log-group-name /vpc/flow/rejects

# Query REJECT records — often SG or NACL mismatch
snippet.explanation: Flow Logs show ACCEPT/REJECT at IP/port level — layer 3–4 evidence when curl times out.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: ALB layer 7 path routing
snippet.code:
Resources:
  ApiListenerRule:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule
    Properties:
      ListenerArn: !Ref HttpsListener
      Priority: 10
      Conditions:
        - Field: path-pattern
          Values: ['/api/*']
      Actions:
        - Type: forward
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref ApiTargetGroup
snippet.explanation: Layer 7 routing inspects HTTP path — Security Groups cannot do path-based routing.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Changing Security Groups when the issue is DNS (layer 7 vs layer 4). Expecting NACL to do path-based routing — that is ALB layer 7. Ignoring TLS layer when HTTP works with -k but fails in browser.

interviewTakeaways: OSI layers map AWS services: VPC/route tables (L3), SG/NACL (L4), TLS/ACM (L6), ALB/Route 53 (L7).
Troubleshoot bottom-up: routing → firewall → TLS → HTTP application.
VPC Flow Logs for L3–4; ALB access logs and curl for L7.
60s: AWS abstracts L1–2. You manage L3 VPC routing, L4 SG ports, L7 ALB HTTP and Route 53 DNS. Peel layers when debugging HTTPS failures.
Follow-up: what is the difference between Security Group and Network ACL?
commonPitfalls: Jumping to application logs when route table has no path — fix L3 before L7.
Strong answer: systematic layer isolation with dig, nc, curl, Flow Logs.
Using NACL for fine-grained app rules — SG is stateful and preferred for instances.
Confusing control plane API errors with data plane connectivity issues.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeError: fetch failed in Node often means DNS (L7) or TCP timeout (L4) — not an HTTP 500. Check layers before blaming application code.
502 Bad Gateway = ALB reached target but got invalid response (L7 app). 503 = no healthy targets (L7 health check / L4 connectivity to target).
